params.body:
The Activiteit screen can say how much was done since 2020, and cannot say how much was *worked*, because the two traces that would answer that overwrite themselves: `vehicles.updated_at` keeps one timestamp no matter how often a car is edited, and `users.last_login_at` keeps one sign-in per user. This adds one row per occurrence for exactly those two.

## Measured before it was built

About 600 handlings and 540 touched vehicles a week, so some two thousand rows a week and a hundred and thirty thousand a year. `vehicle_photos` carries six hundred thousand today, so a year of this is a fifth of that table. Storage was never the question.

## What is deliberately NOT in it

Vehicles, offers, orders, leads, bids and lookups already write themselves down with their own timestamp, reaching back to 2020. Writing them here as well would give the platform two sources for one number, which is how two screens start disagreeing. Photos least of all: 5,157 a week across 174 vehicles, saying nothing the saved car does not already say.

Only what a **person** did is recorded. The photo mill and the scheduled commands also save vehicles, and counting those answers "how busy is the server" instead of "how much is being worked".

## The counts stay out of the totals

This log starts empty. Folded into the handlings it would draw a step on the day of the deploy, and that step reads as growth while it only says we started looking. So it sits in its own block, it names the day it started, and the rule says why. This is the part most likely to be "tidied up" later by someone adding the numbers together.

## Verified

Five tests: three edits give three rows where the column keeps one, a save without a person is not counted, an unwritable log still lets the car be saved, the counts are not folded into the handlings, and the screen names its start date. Checked by mutation — removing the observer hook fails two of them.

Two things about the tests themselves, because both were mistakes I made here first:

- The first version forced the write to fail with `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME`. DDL commits the running transaction in MySQL, so that test leaked its own data into my local database permanently and broke the isolation of seven unrelated tests. It now makes the connection unreachable through config instead.
- The second version forced it with an out-of-range id. Without strict mode MySQL truncates that silently, so the test would have been green here and red elsewhere.

`phpstan` green over the project, `pint` green on the added files. The two existing files are touched by six and seven added lines; no reformatting.

Local suite: the two known `ListPageHeadersTest` cases fail as always, plus seven that fail identically on a clean `main` in my environment — my local database is still carrying the rows the `ALTER TABLE` version leaked, and `IntegrationSmokeTest` additionally reads an `OUTBOUND_IMPACT` from my local `.env`. Neither has anything to do with this change; CI runs on a fresh database and is the judge.

New rule R P3-16.8.
params.title: An event log for what leaves no trace
